generic_inputs.value: Design, but do not yet execute, a historical audit of GeminiSupervisor. Verify in batches that every persisted Supervisor nonce run met the requirements governing that run. Also identify historical user instructions that were never implemented, distinguishing IMPLEMENTED from SUPERSEDED_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION from MISSING_STILL_OUTSTANDING; only MISSING_STILL_OUTSTANDING is a defect. The audit must use commit history, Agents.md, runtime source, Step 3 evaluation/tests, nonce runs, and a verified inventory/definition of what the machine actually is and does today, as opposed to intended or assumed behavior.

evaluation_heuristic: This is a DESIGN-ONLY query. Do not perform the historical audit yet. First define the presently implemented GeminiSupervisor machine from executable evidence: workflows, runtime source, configuration/dependency surfaces, persisted run structure, and current artifacts. Explicitly separate ACTUAL IMPLEMENTED BEHAVIOR from INTENDED CONTRACT in Agents.md and from historical aspirations or assumptions. Then design how a later exhaustive audit should be staged to this evaluator in batches. The audit has two primary objectives: (1) verify every persisted Supervisor nonce run against the requirements and governing implementation that applied when that run occurred; (2) find user instructions that were never implemented, while distinguishing IMPLEMENTED, SUPERSEDED_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION, MISSING_STILL_OUTSTANDING, and INDETERMINATE. Do not call an unimplemented instruction a defect if a later user instruction superseded it before implementation was required. Account for temporal versioning: current Agents.md, source, and Step 3 files cannot automatically govern historical runs. Recommend how to reconstruct the exact or best-supported governing snapshots for each run from Git history and persisted evidence. Decide whether batching should be by contract epoch, chronological run groups, or another method; define exact batch boundaries mechanically. For each proposed batch, specify exactly which files, commit snapshots, and run-container files must be fed to the evaluator and which evidence is authoritative for user requirement, implementation state, execution result, supervisory result, and supersession. Define proof rules for determining whether a nonce run met its requirements, separating schema validity, transition correctness, actual requested work completion, deterministic ground-truth evidence, and user-goal satisfaction where evidence exists. Define a supersession algorithm that can trace an instruction from its originating user request through later commits, runs, and instructions without guessing. Define completeness checks proving every nonce run and every relevant instruction was covered exactly once. Recommend intermediate artifacts that should be generated before batch evaluation, including a current-machine inventory/definition and a temporal contract index. Return a concrete staging plan and schemas only; do not modify Supervisor files and do not claim the audit itself has been performed.
